worldcup.title: Six questions facing England as they target next year’s Women’s World Cup
worldcup.summary: Starting positions at centre-back and No 10 are up for grabs, while Sarina Wiegman’s future continues to be in the air England have two jobs to do on Tuesday. The first, avoiding an almighty upset and progressing past Greece on aggregate in their Women’s World Cup playoff to reach a final tie, should be a formality for one of the world’s best-resourced teams. The second, honing their style to play like contenders for next summer’s World Cup in Brazil, is a far trickier but crucial challenge. Friday’s relatively uninspiring 3-1 first-leg victory in Crete left room for improvement and England had plenty to work on as they trained at St George’s Park on Monday under gloomy-looking clouds. More broadly, over the next eight months, there are six questions facing the European champions. Continue reading...

general.title: Esenyurt’ta yorgan imalathanesi alev alev yandı
general.summary: Yangın, saat 22.30 sıralarında Akçaburgaz Mahallesi 3002 Sokak'ta bulunan iş yerinde çıktı. Edinilen bilgiye göre, yorgan üretimi yapılan tek katlı iş yerinde henüz bilinmeyen nedenle çıkan yangını görenler, durumu itfaiye, polis ve sağlık ekiplerine haber verdi. Bu sırada alevler tüm iş yerini sardı. Olay yerine gelen itfaiye ekipleri, yangına farklı noktalardan müdahale etti. Polis ekipleri çevrede önlem alırken, sağlık ekipleri de hazır bekledi. İtfaiye ekiplerinin çalışmasıyla yangın kontrol altına alınarak söndürüldü. Yangın sonrası herhangi bir yaralanma ve can kaybı yaşanmazken, iş yerinde hasar oluştu. İtfaiye ekipleri yangının çıkış sebebini araştırırken, polis ekipleri olayla ilgili inceleme başlattı. general.title: Carrick promises Manchester United will ‘come out fighting’ after sticky start
general.summary: United have endured worst league start since 1986-87 Trip to Atlético in Champions League awaits on Tuesday Manchester United have endured their worst league start in 40 years but Michael Carrick insists he is “loving it”. United arrived in Madrid without Kobbie Mainoo and Luke Shaw, who both picked up knocks in the draw against Tottenham at the weekend, and with the coach admitting that his team are in “a spot”, but he vowed that they would “come out fighting”. Despite collecting just six points in the Premier League so far, Carrick claimed he did not feel under pressure and backed his captain, Bruno Fernandes, who he revealed was still “carrying something”, to rediscover his form. As he talked about building, there was a reminder too of the fact that Arsenal, the champions, finished “seventh or eighth” in Mikel Arteta’s first two seasons. Continue reading...
